mcp.note: REAL, not a scaffold — this repo IS an MCP bridge: a Figma plugin (manifest.json, editorType figma/figjam) talking to a localhost MCP server over bridge-server.js. Outstanding for mcp-maintainer: (1) fuzex-figma-bridge still has no tools.json declaring its surface or `mutates` per tool — the plugin protocol in code.js handles start-server/stop-server/mcp-request/client-connect/client-disconnect/get-server-status/ping, which is transport, not a tool manifest; (2) mcp-server-config.json hardcodes an absolute Windows cwd (C:/Users/izzyw/source/FuzeX) so the config is not portable to any other machine or to CI. The second server, design-frames-service, DOES declare tools.json with `mutates` per tool (services/design-frames-service/mcp/tools.json) — added together with the service in the navigable-frames extraction; see services/design-frames-service/docs/EXTRACTION.md.

portal.reason: FuzeX itself (the Figma/FigJam plugin) still does not register — its UI runs in Figma's plugin sandbox with networkAccess restricted to localhost, so there is no served origin to iframe and no remoteEntry to federate; that part of this note is unchanged. But design-frames-service, its separate network-reachable product surface, now ALSO ships a Module-Federation remote (services/design-frames-service/webapp) reproducing its review UI in React on @izzywdev/fuzefront-design-system — exposed as scope `fuzex`, module `./DesignFramesApp`, served same-origin under /apps/fuzex/remoteEntry.js via the host's reverse proxy, sharing the host's React 19 singleton (NOT an iframe/spa tile). It registers as a portal tile the FuzeFront host mounts directly; the service's REST API (features/flows/frames, openapi.yaml) is unchanged and still consumed over same-origin fetch by that remote. Registration in the app-registry manifest and the reverse-proxy wiring are handled by the orchestrator, not this repo.
